newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala Congress passes amnesty law.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala Congress passes amnesty law.

text.p: An overwhelming majority of Guatemala's legislators passed an amnesty law on Wednesday that opponents warned would let murders and torture committed during the country's long civil war go unpunished.
The law passed on its third reading with 65 votes in favor, eight votes against and seven members absent. A three-hour debate before the vote was closed to the general public to keep out protestors.

"My father died (during the war) and to this day we don't know who is responsible. But even so this leads me to accept that if the people of Guatemala want reconciliation we have to learn to forgive," Congressman Vinicio Villar Anteu of the Christian Democrat party said as he cast his vote for the bill.
The National Reconciliation Law was proposed as part of a peace agreement ending the 36-year-old civil war that left 140,000 Guatemalans dead or "disappeared."
The government promoted the law as a limited amnesty leading up to the signing of a definitive peace treaty to be signed between the government and leftist rebels Dec. 29.

Debate over the law has divided Guatemalans between those who call for justice and those who say the country must forgive and forget. Human rights activists argue the bill does not specifically exclude kidnappings and murders from crimes that would receive amnesty.
